name: The Frederick Thomas household
head: thomas_frederick

arrival.note: Not_later_than precision on the date of his advertisement. A man advertising his own new shop on 8 June 1835 was in Chicago on 8 June 1835; when he came is not stated and the phrase 'New Drug, Medical and Paint Store' suggests recently.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1835-06-08 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

basis.note: data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json#arrival_and_origin.tables.arrival_year_of_the_known_layer, restricted to years at or before 1835.

replaceable_by.match: a dated source that says which year this household came to Chicago

party_size_on_arrival.note: Not attested in anything this project holds.

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says where this household came from

reason_for_coming.value: A mechanic's trade in a town that had few of it
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as barber surgeon, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

basis.note: arrival_fill.trade_reasons.a_mechanics_trade — the head's recorded trade is evidence about this household, and the draw it answered is the reason the record will carry until a source states one.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says why this household came, or a committed source that apportions the town's arrivals between the land sales, the canal and the harbour works

lives_at.note: Not attested in anything this project holds.

works_at.note: data/structures/frederick_thomas_shop.json exists on the strength of this same advertisement.

present_on_scene_date.note: Advertising at Chicago on 8 June 1835, twenty-three days before the scene date, and in business there into 1836.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

persons.name: Frederick Thomas

occupation.note: 'Frederick Thomas, in the American of June 8, 1835, advertised the proprietorship of the Chicago New Drug, Medical and Paint Store, on Water Street, two doors from the American office, near the drawbridge; and also advertised that he performed "bleeding, leeching and tooth-drawing;" thus establishing himself as Chicago's first barber-surgeon' (Andreas, scan p. 955).

workplaces.basis: The register matches the printed name to the town card thomas_frederick (action: enrich), so this is the same person the resident layer already holds. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

persons.note: DOCUMENTED IN THE TOWN THREE WEEKS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE, which almost nobody in this parcel is, and with a self-reported address relative to two other things in this dataset - the American's office and the Dearborn Street drawbridge. He took a partner, Thomas Jenkins, on 11 January 1836 and retired from that partnership on 2 April 1836, so he is continuous through the scene year on both sides.

resident_research.evidence_for: The Encyclopedia of Chicago independently identifies Frederick Thomas as Chicago's first barber-surgeon and a retail druggist in the 1830s, corroborating the unusual combined occupation. The project newspaper corpus remains the stronger path for exact 1835 advertising/address detail.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 30 under 40', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('thomas_frederick:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: THE CLOSEST DOCUMENTED ARRIVAL TO THE SCENE DATE IN THE PARCEL, and a trade the occupation vocabulary had to be widened for. 'Barber-surgeon' is Andreas's own characterisation of a man who sold paint and drew teeth, and it is a period-correct trade in a way that 'pharmacist' or 'dentist' would not be. HIS ADDRESS IS A CHAIN OF LANDMARKS RATHER THAN A LOT: 'on Water Street, two doors from the American office, near the drawbridge' locates him against two structures this dataset already holds, which is the kind of constraint the placement work in K7 can actually use.
